purpose: How uncertain is a calibration process’s variance when only its sample spread is known?
meaning: Square the observed sample spread and multiply by its degrees of freedom. Divide this same numerator by the upper and lower chi-square quantiles in reverse order to obtain a confidence interval for the population variance.

definition.setting: A workshop summarizes repeated cutting errors from a calibration jig by a sample standard deviation s and a reading count n. Square s to show the observed sample variance, then follow the chi-square quantiles into a lower bound L and upper bound U for the unknown process variance. Change the entered spread or the number of readings while keeping that summary-based comparison explicit.

signature.q_U: Numerical chi-square 0.975 quantile for ν degrees of freedom

conditions: Assume independent identically normal cutting errors with one unknown mean and unknown positive population variance. The sample standard deviation uses n−1 in its variance denominator. The central fixed 95% procedure has repeated-sampling coverage under this model; it does not assign posterior probability to the fixed variance or predict the next error. The general formula requires n≥2; these controls use whole n from 6 to 31 and s from 0.25 to 2 mm to keep the fixed variance axis readable. Changing n holds the entered spread fixed rather than generating observations. Chi-square quantiles are evaluated numerically. Unknown σ² has no supplied location, and the observed sample variance s² must not be presented as that unknown parameter.

properties.claim: Square the observed sample spread and multiply by its degrees of freedom. Divide this same numerator by the upper and lower chi-square quantiles in reverse order to obtain a confidence interval for the population variance.
properties.conditions: Assume independent identically normal cutting errors with one unknown mean and unknown positive population variance. The central fixed 95% procedure has repeated-sampling coverage under this model; it does not assign posterior probability to the fixed variance or predict the next error. properties.derivation: For independent normal readings, the variance pivot (n−1)s² divided by the population variance has a chi-square distribution with n−1 degrees of freedom. Its central 0.95 region lies between the 0.025 and 0.975 quantiles. Inverting the two positive inequalities reverses the quantile positions: the larger quantile produces the lower variance endpoint. Square roots of the variance endpoints give the corresponding standard-deviation interval.
